entries.title: Job 5:1
segments:
Answer thee; as a friend and patron, ready to support thy cause. 
 
  The saints; here probably the holy angels. 
 
Men sometimes think that all the good agree in opinion with themselves, and that those who do not are wicked.

entries.title: Job 5:2
segments: Envy; more exactly, indignation.  It is the wrath and indignation of one who rebels against the discipline of God's providence, which Eliphaz means.  These are the means of ruin to the wicked who indulge them.

entries.title: Job 5:3
segments:
Foolish; here, as throughout the book of Job, the foolish are the wicked, who are destitute of true wisdom. 
 
  Suddenly I cursed his habitation; I saw destruction suddenly come upon his habitation, and pronounced it accursed. 
 
It needs no spirit of prophecy to foretell the ruin of such as continue in a course of disobedience to God.

entries.title: Job 5:4
segments: Crushed in the gate; condemned in the place where judgments were issued.

entries.title: Job 5:5
segments: Even out of the thorns; here probably a hedge of thorns intended for the protection of the harvest.

entries.title: Job 5:6
segments:
Cometh not forth of the dust; affliction does not come by chance; it is ordered by God, and therefore should be cheerfully submitted to. 
 
As troubles do not come by chance, but are directed by infinite wisdom and goodness, for most benevolent ends, they should be borne with patience, and cheerful submission to the perfect will of God.

entries.title: Job 5:7
segments: As the sparks fly upward; it is as natural for fallen man to sin and suffer, as for sparks to fly upward.

entries.title: Job 5:8
segments: I would seek unto God; if I were in thy place; thus expressing the duty of all men in affliction.

entries.title: Job 5:12
segments: No wisdom but that which comes from above will guide a man in the path of truth and duty, or ultimately meet with success.

entries.title: Job 5:13
segments:
The wise; the worldly wise. 
 
  The froward; the perverse who disobey God.

entries.title: Job 5:15
segments: The poor; the afflicted, who trust in God.

entries.title: Job 5:17
segments:
Whom God correcteth; and who receives correction in a proper manner. 
 
Trust in God and supreme devotion to him, will sanctify every trial while it lasts, and in due time secure certain, full, and eternal deliverance.

entries.title: Job 5:19
segments: In six troubles--in seven; a definite is here put for a large indefinite number.

entries.title: Job 5:21
segments: Hid; safe, where the scourge of the tongue cannot find thee.  "The scourge of the tongue" represents those false accusations which expose a man to the spoiling of his goods, to imprisonment, and even death.

entries.title: Job 5:23
segments: In league with the stones; they shall not hurt thee.

entries.title: Job 5:24
segments: Not sin; not wander, err, or miss the way to his house, but find it safe as he left it.

entries.title: Job 5:26
segments: In a full age; not meet a premature death.

entries.title: Job 5:27
segments:
We have searched it; learned from observation, that those who feel and act right, are delivered or saved from trouble; and those only continue to be afflicted, who continue to feel and act wrong.  From this Eliphaz would draw the erroneous conclusion, that the continuance of Job's afflictions proved him to be as Satan affirmed, a hypocrite, or a very selfish, wicked man. 
 
Human reason and observation, without revelation, are unsafe guides; and none, unless enlightened by God, will have such views of his character and ways as lead to safety and success.
